conventions.convention: Haar uses N=2^J with J≥1, pair outputs ((u+v)/√2,(u−v)/√2), and output order coarse coefficient followed by details from coarsest to finest. It introduces no padding.
Compact-filter analysis uses x[(2k+j) mod N], g_j=(−1)^j h_{L−1−j}, approximation rows before detail rows, and transpose synthesis. Each applied level has even current length at least 2L.
The D4 multilevel transform has J≥3 and stops at four coarse coefficients after J−2 stages. Periodic reduction uses each stage's current length.
The smooth class requires C^q regularity on an open interval containing [0,1]; M_r bounds derivatives on [0,1]. It does not claim to exhaust W^{q,∞}.
Cell averages use J≥0 and half-open dyadic cells for point values; the value at 1 is the last cell's average.
Hard retention keeps m largest absolute coefficients with arbitrary tie resolution, including m=0,N. Soft thresholding uses λ≥0 and sign(0)=0 and does not prescribe a retained count.

The finite Besov quantity includes four coarse coefficients and detail blocks of size 2^j for 2≤j≤J−1. At p=(s+1/2)^{-1}, it equals the full coefficient ℓ^p quasi-norm; no intrinsic function-space norm equivalence is asserted.
The sampled D4 estimate requires a globally 1-periodic C^2 function and normalized samples x_n=N^{-1/2}f(n/N); detail scale j equals J−ℓ.
For a finite Riesz synthesis matrix, coefficients are V^{-1}x and synthesis is Vc; positive bounds A,B control squared Euclidean norms.

load_bearing.statement: For every admissible pair (h,g), every even N≥2L, and every x∈R^N, the analysis matrix W is orthogonal, synthesis W^T is its inverse, and ‖Wx‖₂²=‖x‖₂². Every defined multilevel transform is orthogonal, with inverse obtained by reversing stages and applying their transposes.
The explicit D4 pair is admissible, and Σ j^r g_j=0 for r=0,1, so its high-pass filter annihilates constant and affine data.

At stage ℓ, the D4 detail block has 2^{J−ℓ} translates. Each row has support within at most 3(2^ℓ−1)+1 consecutive lifted input indices, Euclidean norm 1, affine cancellation on that lift, and ℓ¹ norm at most the square root of its support size. For 1≤ℓ≤J−2 the support interval has fewer than N indices.

For orthogonal U, c=Ux, and any retained set S, ‖x−U^T P_Sc‖₂²=Σ_{i∉S}|c_i|². For every 0≤m≤N, retaining m largest absolute coefficients minimizes reconstruction error among choices retaining at most m coefficients.

For J≥3, N=2^J, s>0, p=(s+1/2)^{-1}∈(0,2), orthogonal U and c=Ux partitioned into the stated coarse and detail blocks, hard retention satisfies ‖x−U^T H_m(c)‖₂≤√(p/(2−p)) ‖c‖_{b^s_{p,p}(J)} m^{-s} for 1≤m≤N.
For J≥3 and normalized samples of a 1-periodic C^2 function, every multilevel D4 detail coefficient at scale j=J−ℓ satisfies |d_{j,k}|≤(9√3/2)M₂ 2^{-5j/2}.
For every J≥1, the finite periodic Haar transform is an orthogonal linear map, its inverse is its transpose, and it preserves squared Euclidean norm.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite real coordinate inner products and squared Euclidean norms in transform orthogonality, thresholding, and Riesz-tail arguments.
The derivative and C^q conventions underlying the smooth derivative-bound class.
Its n=0 case gives the cellwise Lipschitz increment estimate; its n=1 case gives the quadratic remainder after affine cancellation in the sampled D4 estimate.

concerns.concern: Step 1.1 says that at the displayed index t, “its coefficient is” g_r times the product of the h_{s_v}. Different tuples can produce the same t, so an effective row entry is the sum of those products. Already at ℓ=2, t=2 receives both (r,s₁)=(0,2) and (1,0), giving g₀h₂+g₁h₀, rather than either individual product. The support, moment and normalization conclusions remain valid after explicitly accumulating coincident contributions; the current coefficient description omits that summation.
